title: Reducing Authorship Attribution Risk in Student Texts Through Style-Conditioned Rewriting
abstract: arXiv:2611.29642v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Building NLP applications for education is constrained by data scarcity due to student privacy concerns and data regulations. To address this, we propose a style-aware approach to rewriting student forum posts that retains analytical value while reducing identifiability. Our method isolates content, structure, and style as separate conditioning channels and aggregates over student-disjoint exemplar partitions within style clusters, extending Differentially Private In-context Learning (DP-ICL) with cluster-restricted retrieval. Across three educational NLP datasets, our approach achieves high style fidelity, preserves downstream task performance, and reduces authorship attribution risk relative to the original student-written texts, including against a dedicated authorship-attribution model.

translated_title: 通过风格条件化改写降低学生文本的作者归属风险
translated_abstract: 由于学生隐私担忧和数据法规的限制，构建面向教育的NLP应用受到数据稀缺的制约。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种风格感知的方法来改写学生论坛帖子，在降低可识别性的同时保留分析价值。我们的方法将内容、结构和风格作为独立的条件化通道进行隔离，并在风格聚类内的学生不相交示例分区上进行聚合，通过聚类受限检索扩展了差分隐私上下文学习（DP-ICL）。在三个教育NLP数据集上，我们的方法实现了高风格保真度，保留了下游任务性能，并相对于原始学生撰写文本降低了作者归属风险，包括在面对专门的作者归属模型时也表现有效。
tldr: 该论文提出一种风格感知的改写方法，通过将内容、结构与风格解耦并结合聚类受限检索的差分隐私上下文学习（DP-ICL），在保留文本分析价值和下游任务性能的同时，有效降低学生文本的作者归属风险。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a style-aware rewriting approach that isolates content, structure, and style as separate conditioning channels and extends DP-ICL with cluster-restricted retrieval, reducing authorship attribution risk in student texts while preserving analytical value and downstream task performance.
